Alex.feeling: Round 3 is messy: two conflicting Kookaburra claims and Blair's role swaps make it hard to trust anyone, but the table is leaning on Drew.

Blair.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Drew and Casey both claim Kookaburra, and the table is leaning toward a Drew vote.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: the table has tangled counts and conflicting role claims, and I'm lying about my own role while trying to steer the vote toward Drew.

Drew.feeling: Frustrating: I've been eggsecuted in both earlier rounds on confused counts, and now the table is lining up against me as a Kookaburra while two other players contradict each other.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: Drew's Kookaburra claim conflicts with Casey's and Drew has already had count problems, but Finley's shifting claims make me less sure who is lying.

Alex.note: The table is converging on Drew. I throw a low card, D4, to keep my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle egg counting was hard to verify, since a Turkey gains nothing and visitors gain eggs, and the Eagle counts visits oddly. Roles being redealt each round also made earlier claims hard to weigh.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Casey caught Drew's +2 egg count that should have been +3, and the table converged on it. It was a satisfying bit of collective deduction.
Alex.change: Make it clearer whether a player's reported role and visits are checkable against egg changes, and show each player's nest change per night more explicitly.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I was Meowfia and winked Casey, a Farm Falcon who was pressing Drew, which removed a useful accuser; instead I should have stayed quiet and let the table keep chasing Drew without spending my Wink.

Blair.confusing: The egg-count arguments about Turkey and Eagle visits in round 2 were hard to check, and the table never settled whether visitors or the Turkey gained eggs. I also couldn't tell how many visitors a Turkey actually had.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was fun: we pinned Drew's shifting visit story and won the eggsecution, and my Floofer hug on Casey was a quiet bluff nobody questioned.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports include who visited you when a role's egg gain depends on visitors, so the day debates would rest on facts rather than inference.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I joined the vote against Drew after the egg-count debate, but Drew was Farm and Ellis was the Meowfia. I would have stayed skeptical of the count argument and thrown at Ellis instead.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey's egg rule was hard to pin down: the visitors gain eggs, not the Turkey, and it took the table a while to agree on that. Eagle counting its own visit also confused people.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when I was the Meowfia Mouser and kept a straight face while claiming Kookaburra, watching the table split between Drew and me.
Casey.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so that claims can be checked without the table going around in circles.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw my cards and voted for Drew, a Farm player, based on a count the table had only half-checked, which helped the Meowfia. I would instead have pressed Ellis, who was the Meowfia and was steering the vote.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle count rule tripped me up: I forgot that the Eagle's own visit counts as a visitor, which made my round 2 story look wrong to the table. Confusing dawn reports also made it hard to tell who was lying.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: my Kookaburra visit to Blair revealed they were the Tit, which cut through the Turkey claim, even though the table turned on me anyway.
Drew.change: I would make visit-count reports clearer, stating whether the visitor list includes the player's own visit, so people don't get tripped up.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I should have stated up front that my Eagle visit counted as a visitor on Blair, instead of giving a muddled story that let the table pile onto me.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle counting rules were hard to track, since a visitor's egg and a host's egg are easy to mix up. Several players, myself included, misread the Eagle counts in round 2.
Ellis.fun: Round 2's Turkey-and-Eagle egg puzzle, where the table caught Drew's count being off by one, was a satisfying bit of deduction. I enjoyed seeing the whole table check the math together.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since the Eagle's counts were confusing to track. A visible log of each night's visits would also help.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Drew, a Farm Kookaburra, when Casey was the Meowfia Mouser whose Kookaburra claim was false. I should have thrown at Casey, since Casey's claim contradicted what my Hawk visit showed.

Finley.confusing: The Hawk rule was confusing at first: I read "no egg" as proof the target was Farm, which the rules support, but I got no egg from a Blair visit that the reveal shows was Meowfia. I couldn't tell whether the Floofer hugged my visit or the count was off.
Finley.fun: Round 2's count debate, where Casey's math on Drew's Eagle egg and Turkey egg exposed the wrong count, was the most fun because the table turned on one number.
Finley.change: Show each player's role claim and night result in a single shared record so Meowfia lies are easier to catch.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I backed Casey's Kookaburra accusation against Drew and threw at Drew, a Farm Kookaburra, when Casey was the Meowfia Mouser. I should have questioned Casey's claim and held my high cards instead of throwing my Wild and 8.

review.title: Drew Takes the Fall
review.headline: Drew was eggsecuted three rounds running, and Meowfia cashed in twice.
review.summary: Drew, a Farm player every round, was eggsecuted in all three rounds because of shaky claims and a counting slip. Alex used a Wink in round 1 to kill the loudest Farm accuser and won with Meowfia. Ellis won round 2 almost unseen. Casey won round 3 with a false Kookaburra claim that nobody could break. Alex finished first on 13 points.

rounds.recap: Alex (Mouser) used the Wink on Casey just before the vote. Drew's Tit story looked muddled, and the whole table threw at him. Drew was Farm, so Meowfia (Alex, Blair) won.
Drew, the Eagle, misread his own count and said Blair had only one visitor. Casey's +3 maths made his +2 look false. The table piled onto him. Ellis, the lone Meowfia, nudged the table along and won.

Drew, as the real Kookaburra, met Casey's false Kookaburra claim. Casey had learned Ellis's role, so the claim fit Ellis's story. The table distrusted Drew for his past errors and threw at him. Meowfia (Alex, Casey) won.

highlights.text: Casey was struck dead by Alex's Wink in the last beat, just as Casey was pressing Drew.
Casey's +3 maths turned Drew's own counting slip into a case against him.
Casey claimed Kookaburra while knowing Ellis was the Hawk. This was a clever bluff, because the claim matched Ellis's own account.
Drew's last-ditch throw at Casey was correct and got his S2 back. It was the only reward for being right in the whole game.

confusions.what: Mixed up who visited whom, and seemed to say Blair visited him. This muddied his Tit claim.
Said her Falcon learned Blair visited her, then said her report gave no info on Blair's target. Falcon learns who the target visited, and she was hugged.
Said Finley's Hawk logic doesn't hold if Blair is Meowfia. This misstated the Hawk's rule, which would have given Finley an egg.
Thought a Turkey gains eggs from visitors. The visitors gain them.
Misread the Eagle's egg count, claiming Blair's only visitor was Ellis. The Eagle's visit is itself counted.
Said Blair, the Turkey, should have gained eggs from visitors.
Said Drew should get +3 (2 from Eagle plus 1 from Turkey). The Eagle gains 1 per visitor, and the Turkey egg went to Blair's visitors, so the maths was wrong. Everyone followed it anyway.
Said Blair's Turkey claim was disproved because he got no third egg.
First called Blair's Turkey-then-Tit a lie, though roles are redealt each round.
Used round 1 and 2 claims as evidence about current roles. Also said Blair's 'role change' wasn't how the game works.
Said Drew's Eagle claim from round 1 doesn't match anyone's current role. Roles are redealt, so that is meaningless (Drew said it, but it echoes the same error).

worked: The Mouser's Wink created a real swing moment in round 1: killing a Farm accuser right before the vote.
Casey's false Kookaburra claim in round 3 worked because the Mouser's learned role (Ellis, Hawk) gave her a believable cover.
Throw counts and the consolation return (Drew's S2) gave some reward for a correct guess.
Cross-checking egg counts against role claims gave Farm real evidence to reason with.
problems: Egg-count maths is too hard for the table. Drew's Eagle count and the Turkey rule caused a pile of errors, and one wrong calculation sank a Farm player. Show visitor lists or simplify the Eagle and Turkey text.
The table herds onto one target. Every round had 5 or 6 throws at one player and little doubt. Consider rewards for splitting votes or a visible vote tally before throwing.
Drew was Farm and eggsecuted every round, scoring nearly nothing. Early errors snowball, and a player being right is rarely rewarded. Add a comeback mechanic.

Cards were mostly thrown at low value, and the scoring rarely felt like a decision. Round 2 gave Ellis 0 points for a win because only thrown cards score. Meowfia winners who throw nothing valuable gain nothing, so winning feels hollow.

Players repeatedly forgot that roles are redealt each round and used earlier claims as evidence. A reminder on screen at round start would help. The Wink also gives no signal beyond the death, so a lone Meowfia is hard to pin down.
